additional_info.subject: RE: ID0378063-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / S5 170003680] Charging interruption. CRM:00643000899
additional_info.body:
Hi Thomas,
We have analysed all the logs & below are some references snapshot form the charging session.  The logs I’ve shared below demonstrate that the EV functions as the Master & charger functions as Slave. The charger provided the current and voltage that the EV demanded.
As you can see from the multiple session logs, the EV’s target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to 80% SOC using CC, and then it switches to CV mode gradually based on EV requirements. During this phase, the EV's target current drops to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing.
Transaction Id: 201271307
The charging session was started when EV SOC: 38% and ended around EV SOC was 100%.
Transaction Id: 201671524
The charging session was started when EV SOC: 48% and ended around EV SOC was 100%. 7
Based on this analysis, we conclude that there is no issue with the EVSE. I hope this addresses your concerns. If there are no further questions, shall we proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
